disclosures.when: 2026-10-19 (first sealed run aborted in --grade; corrected before any re-run)
disclosures.what: The first sealed run completed all arms but --grade crashed (globbed disclosures.json as a ResultsFile). Inspecting the arm outputs revealed THREE harness bugs (all in eval/sealed_run.py, none in the engine): (1) top-1 / false-confident / ECE were scored on candidates[0], which the frozen engine leaves in the RECTIFIED frame, while only LocalizeResult.offset is mapped back to native coords -- understating v2 on the rotated tiers (nominal/hard); (2) set-recall used the engine's returned top-K instead of the generation set-recall defined in eval/gate_g2.py; (3) the --grade glob tried to parse non-ResultsFile sidecars. Additionally the v1 arm was invoking v1's default (NCC-like) candidate source, making it identical to ncc; corrected to the true v1 LATTICE path (candidate_source='lattice') per the protocol, with ncc kept as the NCC-path baseline.
disclosures.why_no_influence: These are measurement/reporting choices in eval/sealed_run.py, not engine changes; the engine stayed SHA-frozen at f9395b84 and deterministic (git diff over driftsense/, localization/, data_gen/, config.py, contracts.py, api.py is empty between the pin and the harness branch). The fixes (top-1 from native offset; set-recall via gate_g2._set_recall; grade glob skips sidecars; v1 lattice path) were validated on the DEV set before the re-run (run 2). Run 2 then surfaced a further v1-arm bug -- see the next disclosure.

disclosures.when: 2026-10-19 (second sealed run completed; corrected before the third/final run)
disclosures.what: The second (corrected) sealed run completed with exit 0, but the v1 arm scored top-1 = 0.000 on every tier (clean included, where ncc scores 0.975). Cause (eval/sealed_run.py only): v1's localizer returns its lattice candidates in replica/generation order, NOT ranked, and its authoritative pick is pred_x/pred_y = max(candidates, key=combined). The v1 arm wrapper used candidates[0] -- a fixed-position replica near (935,935) -- as the committed point. Fixed to rank candidates by combined score and take the committed point from pred_x/pred_y (native centre, subpixel). The v1 candidate positions were already in native coordinates; only the candidate SELECTION was wrong, not the frame.
disclosures.why_no_influence: A harness-side candidate-selection fix in eval/sealed_run.py; the engine stayed SHA-frozen at f9395b84 (git diff over driftsense/, localization/, data_gen/, config.py, contracts.py, api.py remained empty). The bug was found and fixed WITHOUT any sealed label: it was diagnosed and verified entirely on DEV (v1 lattice pred_x/pred_y hits 12/12 clean DEV pairs vs candidates[0] 0/12; full-DEV v1 top1 clean 0.975 / nominal 0.850 / hard 0.400 / ambiguous 0.000). The fix added a self-test assertion (v1 clean top1 >= 0.8 on DEV) that the old 'v1 != ncc' check missed. Before the third run a proactive cross-arm audit confirmed EVERY arm (ncc, v1, v2_single, all six ablation rungs, both agent arms) scores top-1 from the engine's ranked native prediction (not candidates[0], not rectified coordinates) and that set-recall uses the gate_g2 generation definition throughout; all six ablation rungs localize 8/8 on DEV clean. The committed sealed numbers come from the third run with this audited harness.
disclosures.report_limitation_line: The sealed-eval harness (never the engine) was corrected over three runs; the engine was SHA-frozen at v2-freeze (f9395b84) throughout and every harness bug was found and fixed on the DEV set, so no sealed label influenced any result.
